chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.

15.original: [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.]
15.content: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.

spiritual_reading:
A certain teacher magnifies himself from his own understanding, and from that self-derived speech he produces what is harmful. From this arise parties and divisions in doctrine. Yet when they try to describe the two fundamental principles of human life as if they were one mixed thing in the natural degree, they stumble; for they judge spiritual realities by external appearance, and therefore make what is from heaven seem blended with what is from hell. In that confused view they choose some single instance from outward life and call it the whole, not seeing that in a mixed state not every least thing is of one quality.

For in the regenerate and in the unregenerate there is at first an intermixture in the outermost degree, and one thing seems to strike and determine another; and while the process continues, something of one origin appears within the activities and extensions of life, and something of the other origin appears there also. Thus there is in the natural degree a clinging obscurity that makes evil look like good and good look like evil. Yet the judgment of heaven is not made from that obscurity; for the decision is made from the reigning love and its end, and from the order of influx that follows it. Therefore they err who name what is from heaven by the name of what is from the proprium, or name what is from the proprium by the name of what is from heaven, and then persuade themselves that because something feels pleasant to the natural mind it is therefore living good. They take what nourishes the external man and declare it to be what nourishes the internal man, and so they teach that what is merely natural delight may be joined with the life of heaven and be called spiritual.

Now it shall be opened how the true expositor of these two principles speaks. The Divine Itself, the source of all, provides all things by orderly influx in every degree of the created universe. There is in that order a heavenly origin of life that is wholly good, and from it there is wisdom that enlightens. The power that upholds and establishes heaven in ultimates is from that same origin.

Those who are in understanding are invested with forms suited to their state in the natural degree, and yet within those forms are interior principles of light that have been mixed into the whole by the Divine, so that the total human can be reformed and made one.

This is the heavenly origin of life in its manifested form.

It is now revealed that within it there is a sufficient fullness for all the work of regeneration, arranged in a complete series. First is the reception that begins in the external community of those who are being gathered into good. Second is the confirming power that makes good steadfast and gives it permanence in ultimates through conjunction with heaven. Third is the first combatant good that enters against evil by means of truths, and carries life through temptations by the understanding enlightened from within. Fourth is the mediating operation that brings a clearer light, distinguishing day from night, and leading by a higher wisdom in the spiritual degree. Fifth is the Divine Itself, above all, the infinite source, perfect in all the heavens of light.

The ascent of regeneration is according to this order. The first reception lifts a person from mere natural life into the beginnings of the church within; from this he is raised to confirming power, by which he is held in the order of heaven; then he is raised to combatant good, where he is instructed and defended in states of obscurity; from there he rises into the mediating wisdom that enlightens the understanding in states of clarity; and that glorious mediating wisdom leads him into the acknowledgment and conjunction with the Divine Itself, which is Truth itself and the one Mind from which all the heavens have their glory.

From this heavenly origin comes every good work; and the good that proceeds is the whole of spiritual life and spiritual illumination to eternity. Insofar as it is received it is blessed, because it is the Divine in operation within a created subject.

But there is also a hellish origin of life, which appears in the natural degree by the same outward forms, and therefore deceives. It works by self-love, by dominion from that love, and by the turning of heavenly order into a rotating compulsion that carries the mind in circles. In the outermost life it produces a sufficient fullness of sensual and bodily cravings that walk as if they were living principles, and from these proceed works that imitate goods but are in themselves falsified teachings and persuasive errors, the hidden device that the adversary of heaven sets within the world.

The delight of these evil works is the delight of evil people and of divided doctrines that bind the mind under rule after rule without inner life. They and their leaders make a covenant with what is dead, accepting and loving it, thirsting for it as if it were truth. Thus they become forms of spiritual death.

It is also revealed that this hellish origin has a sufficient fullness arranged in its own series, mirroring the order of heaven but inverted. First is an external reception of falsity, the ruling doctrine of spiritual death from which the divided teachings draw their instruction. Second is the confirming of that falsity by continual shifting of persuasions, so that the mind passes from one appearance to another and never comes to rest in truth. Third is the fierce lust of destroying good and truth, in which self-love burns and casts up dense obscurity, so that the understanding is suffocated and made insane. Fourth is the plotting and reasoning from falsity that forms a containing structure for deception, by which evils are made to seem allowable and even wise. Fifth is the final state in which evil and falsity are conjoined into one hardened mass of confirmation, the last bond that closes the interiors, so that what the adversary has rejected from heaven is gathered into a single fixed form. Then the mind falls into the denial of good, and into total falsity, and whatever remains of truth is taken away. Thus it is absorbed into that hardened confirmation and bound in it; and the works that proceed are works of darkness, persisting to eternity. Whoever comes into that state comes to a place within himself where there is no turning back, because there is no longer any will for repentance.

This, then, is the opening of the hellish origin, as it has been explained: it produces works that appear like goods for a time in outward life, yet in their inner quality are evil, and in every stage of their existence they carry their own end within them.

Concerning this, the beloved are to be held in truth: heavenly good is from a wholly good origin and is capable of being made living and luminous in the natural degree, so that death and darkness are not within it. But the hellish origin is from the ultimate proprium separated from heaven, and in it alone are generated spiritual darkness and spiritual death.

Blessed is everyone who discerns these two origins and separates them in thought and life. He understands that they do not spring from each other, nor do they come forth one out of the other, nor are they from a single mixed source. Whoever can make this separation in himself can be raised into the heaven of light, as has been revealed.

Then he sees that evil works do not arise from heavenly good, nor can they be born from it. But whoever will not separate these origins within himself, and confounds what is from heaven with what is from hell, falls into the state of darkness and remains there until he comes into the final fixation of his ruling love.

Blessed is whoever can believe this in heart and understanding; for he is delivered from falsity and the evil life that proceeds from it, which otherwise would persist with him to eternity.

assessment: Most lacunae can be constrained at the level of doctrinal structure: two discrete origins, outward similarity in the natural degree, and the fivefold series for each tree with ascent and inversion. Exact phrasing at several early ¶6 and ¶19 gaps remains uncertain because the surviving natural text gives only short syntactic anchors; restorations there follow the correspondential necessities (mixture in ultimates, judgment from taste, self-love and dominion, wheel-compulsion, final lump and last bond) in the oldest impersonal cosmological register.
